channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Hugo Motta diz que vê de forma positiva escolha de Guimarães para SRI
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta praised President Lula's appointment of federal deputy José Guimarães (PT) to lead the Secretariat of Institutional Relations (SRI), calling it a positive development. The statement was made to Broadcast Político on Saturday, April 11.

item.title: O otimismo de Jorge Messias com a sabatina no Senado
item.description: Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee for the Supreme Court, expresses optimism ahead of his Senate confirmation hearing on April 29, noting growing support even among opposition senators. He says he is confident in his work at the AGU and pleased with the reception among lawmakers. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded the nomination to the CCJ, with Senator Weverton Rocha as rapporteur.

item.title: TSE deve publicar 2ª-feira acórdão sobre governo do Rio sem decisão sobre nova eleição
item.description: The TSE is set to publish on Monday, the 13th, the ruling that annulled the mandate of Rio de Janeiro Governor Cláudio Castro. The decision allows the STF to resume voting on how the next governor of the state will be chosen, without yet determining whether a new election will be held.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende ajuste fiscal
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, defended the need for a fiscal adjustment in response to rising household debt in Brazil, during an interview in Porto Alegre on Saturday, the 11th. He argued that controlling public spending is essential to stabilize the economy and ease pressure on citizens. The remarks came amid growing concerns over household indebtedness and inflation.

item.title: Levantamento revela que 6x1 melhora imagem de Lula nas redes, mas tema perde de longe para Lulinha e Master
item.description: The debate over ending the 6x1 work schedule improves Lula's digital exposure quality by approximately 30%, while associations with Banco Master and news about Lulinha negatively impact his image by 67% and 74%, respectively. Although the labor topic has a positive effect, it is outweighed in negative relevance by scandals involving Lula's family and financial institutions linked to the government.

item.title: Lula escolhe José Guimarães para vaga de Gleisi em ministério
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) appointed federal deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE), the government leader in the Chamber of Deputies, as the new minister of the Secretariat of Institutional Relations, replacing Gleisi Hoffmann. Guimarães confirmed his swearing-in for next Tuesday (14) via social media, citing a direct invitation from the president. His main responsibility will be political articulation with Congress.

item.title: Líder do PSB, que apoia Haddad, elogia Tarcísio em Campinas; veja vídeo
item.description: PSB leader in the Chamber, federal deputy Jonas Donizette, praised Governor Tarcísio de Freitas during an event in Campinas, highlighting his administration's actions. The unexpected endorsement comes despite the PSB normally supporting Fernando Haddad in the 2026 elections. The gesture was captured on video and reported by local media.

item.title: Motta vê escolha de novo ministro da articulação política como ‘positiva’ e diz que vai se reunir com Lula
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta praised the appointment of José Guimarães as the new Minister of Institutional Relations, calling it 'positive' and citing his experience and moderation. Motta said he will be consulted by the government on the selection of the new government leader in the Chamber and plans to meet with Lula to discuss issues such as the 6x1 work scale change and the regulation of app-based work.

item.title: Acampamento Terra Livre termina com pedido para acelerar demarcações
item.description: The Terra Livre Camp, attended by over 7,000 Indigenous people from all regions, concluded with a call to accelerate the demarcation of Indigenous territories in Brazil. Dinamam Tuxá of Apib criticized the slow pace of the Executive Branch in demarcating and protecting lands, despite acknowledging 20 territories demarcated in the last three years. Threats such as the marco temporal (PEC 48) and Bill 6050, which aim to open Indigenous lands to large enterprises, were denounced, as well as the Ferrogrão railway, which threatens the Jamanxim National Park.

item.title: Empresário bolsonarista ligado a atos de 8 de janeiro é detido por imigração nos Estados Unidos
item.description: Bolsonarist businessman Esdras Jônatas dos Santos, investigated for involvement in the January 8, 2023, coup attempt, was detained by ICE in the United States. He was subject to an arrest warrant in Brazil for organizing anti-democratic demonstrations in Minas Gerais following the 2022 elections, including military barracks encampments and the occupation of Avenida Raja Gabaglia in Belo Horizonte. Although detained, his deportation is not automatic and will be determined by U.S. immigration courts based on his migratory status and any requests from Brazilian authorities.

item.title: TSE planeja publicar segunda-feira acórdão sobre governo do Rio sem decisão sobre nova eleição
item.description: The TSE will publish on Monday the acórdão that cassated Cláudio Castro's mandate, without addressing the succession in Rio de Janeiro. The STF will resume voting on how to choose the next governor after the case is released, depending on its inclusion in the agenda by President Edson Fachin. So far, four ministers have voted for indirect election via Alerj and one for direct election, with five still to vote.

item.title: José Guimarães assume lugar de Gleisi na articulação política do governo
item.description: Federal Deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE) will assume the Secretariat of Institutional Relations in the federal government, replacing Gleisi Hoffmann, who left the post to run for Senate in Paraná. Guimarães, who previously led the government’s bloc in the Chamber of Deputies, abandoned his electoral candidacy this year to take the position, with swearing-in scheduled for Tuesday, the 14th, although the Planalto Palace has not yet officially confirmed the appointment.

item.title: Lula escolhe José Guimarães como novo articulador político
item.description: President Lula appointed José Guimarães (PT-CE), the government leader in the Chamber of Deputies, as the new minister of the Secretariat of Institutional Relations (SRI), with inauguration scheduled for April 14, 2025. Guimarães replaces Gleisi Hoffmann, who stepped down to run for Senate in 2026. His appointment aims to strengthen governability amid challenges such as ending the 6×1 work schedule and Lula’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which Congress will vote on April 30.

item.title: Datafolha: a maior força política do Brasil hoje é o antipetismo
item.description: Datafolha indicates that anti-PT sentiment is Brazil's strongest political force today, with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro leading the presidential race due to his surname and opposition to the PT. Lula has 48% disapproval, while Flávio has 46%, reflecting a 'duel of rejections'. Although Caiado and Zema have low rejection rates (16% and 17%), they remain unknown to about half the electorate and have not yet reached double digits in voting intentions.

item.title: Lula escolhe José Guimarães como sucessor de Gleisi na articulação política
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has selected federal deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE) as the new Minister of Institutional Relations, replacing Gleisi Hoffmann, who stepped down to comply with candidacy disqualification rules ahead of the October 2026 elections. Guimarães’ swearing-in is scheduled for next Tuesday, April 14. A five-term federal deputy, Guimarães is notably the author of a bill seeking to criminalize fatphobia in Brazil.

item.title: Flávio celebra vantagem numérica sobre Lula no Datafolha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated the Datafolha poll results showing him ahead of President Lula in a hypothetical 2026 election runoff. He emphasized the early stage of the campaign and expressed optimism on social media.

item.title: Carluxo critica “inércia” de Valdemar
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro, former city councilman and pre-candidate for the Senate, publicly criticized PL president Valdemar Costa Neto for alleged inaction in Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign. In a social media post, nicknamed 'Carluxo,' he urged greater party involvement, saying: 'Valdemar, help me help you, before it's too late...' The criticism highlights internal tensions within the PL regarding its 2026 electoral strategy.

item.title: Deputado José Guimarães (PT-CE) assumirá a Secretaria de Relações Institucionais
item.description: Federal deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE) will assume as minister of the Secretariat of Institutional Relations in the Lula government on Tuesday, the 14th, replacing Gleisi Hoffmann. He had been the government’s leader in the Chamber of Deputies since the start of the administration and will face key challenges including regulating app-based work and ending the 6x1 work scale. Hoffmann is leaving the post to run for Senate in Paraná in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Caiado segue mais perto de Daciolo que de Lula e Flávio nas pesquisas
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the former governor of Goiás and PSD's presidential pre-candidate for 2026, polls at 5% in voting intentions according to a Datafolha survey, far behind Lula (39%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (35%). Despite the low numbers, PSD president Gilberto Kassab stated that 15% would be an 'excellent' result for Caiado. Caiado is technically tied with low-polling candidates such as Romeu Zema, Renan Santos, Aldo Rebelo, and Cabo Daciolo.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula tem 48% de rejeição, contra 46% de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula has 48% rejection, making him the most rejected presidential pre-candidate in the polls, according to Datafolha. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), the president's main adversary, records 46% rejection, just two points behind. The survey, released on January 11, indicates a highly polarized scenario for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que, se vencer, subirá rampa do Planalto com pai
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, stated that if he wins the 2026 election, he will ascend the Planalto ramp for his inauguration accompanied by his father, Jair Bolsonaro. This action depends on a change in the former president’s legal status, who is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence under house arrest.

item.title: Governo vai implantar sistema de chamadas verificadas contra fraudes telefônicas
item.description: The Lula government announced the implementation of a verified call system to combat phone fraud and protect citizens' sensitive information. The measure aims to reduce scams such as fake bank calls and improper extraction of personal data.

item.title: Entenda o acordo entre Brasil e EUA sobre o crime organizado
item.description: Brazil and the United States formalized the MIT Project agreement to enhance cooperation against transnational organized crime, focusing on tracking illicit arms and drugs. The initiative enables real-time intelligence sharing between Brazil’s Federal Revenue and U.S. Customs and Border Protection via the DESARMA digital platform. The Brazilian government stresses the pact is unrelated to potential U.S. designation of Brazilian factions as 'narcoterrorists,' a claim rejected by President Lula.

item.title: Novo Datafolha: como fica a disputa de rejeição entre Lula, Flávio, Caiado e Zema
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows Lula (48%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (46%) leading in rejection rates, with slight increases since March, while Zema (17%) and Caiado (16%) show significantly lower rejection. In hypothetical second-round scenarios, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied (46% to 45%), and Lula also ties with Zema and Caiado, underscoring persistent polarization. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters across 137 municipalities between April 7 and 9.

item.title: Lula lidera rejeição entre pré-candidatos, aponta Datafolha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leads in rejection among 2026 presidential pre-candidates, with 48% of voters saying they would not vote for him, closely followed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) at 46%, within the margin of error. Both are also the most recognized: Lula by 81% and Flávio by 58%. Other candidates show rejection rates between 10% and 19%.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro lideram índice de rejeição por eleitores, diz Datafolha
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro lead rejection rates among presidential pre-candidates, with 48% and 46% respectively, according to a Datafolha poll. Both are also the most recognized candidates, with 61% and 34% of voters saying they know them very well. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters between April 7 and 9, 2026.

item.title: Datafolha aponta rejeição de 48% para Lula, 46% para Flávio, 17% para Zema e 16% para Caiado
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on April 11 shows President Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tied in rejection for a potential 2026 presidential runoff, at 48% and 46% respectively. Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) have lower rejection rates at 17% and 16%, but low name recognition, with 56% and 54% of voters saying they don’t know who they are. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters aged 16 or older between April 7 and 9, with a margin of error of two percentage points and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula perde vantagem e empata com Flávio Bolsonaro em eventual 2º turno
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has lost his lead in potential second-round scenarios and is now technically tied with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), according to a Datafolha poll. For the first time, the opponent numerically surpasses the incumbent in voting intentions for a potential 2026 presidential runoff.

item.title: Acampamento indígena em Brasília anuncia apoio à reeleição de Lula, mas aponta contradições
item.description: Indigenous organizations gathered at the Free Land Camp in Brasília announced support for Lula's re-election, but pointed out persistent contradictions in his policies, particularly criticizing oil exploration in the Amazon River mouth as harmful to indigenous territories and communities.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro entre católicos e evangélicos, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: According to a Datafolha poll released on April 11, 2026, Lula leads among Catholic voters with 43% voting intention, compared to 30% for Flávio Bolsonaro, while Flávio leads among evangelicals with 49%, versus 25% for Lula. Overall, Lula has 39% and Flávio 35%, technically tied within the margin of error. In a projected runoff, Flávio leads with 46% and Lula with 45%, also a technical tie.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 46% e Lula, 45%, no segundo turno
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula in a hypothetical runoff with 46% to 45%, within the margin of error — the first time the senator has surpassed the president in this institute’s survey. Although Lula still holds a first-round lead (38% to 32%), his advantage has narrowed from 15 points in December to just six, signaling significant electoral volatility. The poll also reveals widespread distrust in institutions, with 69% of respondents expressing insecurity about the electoral process.

item.title: Lula empata com Flávio, Zema e Caiado em 2º turno, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on Saturday, the 11th, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a technical tie in various second-round scenarios for the 2026 elections. For the first time, he is numerically surpassed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with 46% against Lula's 45%. The survey also indicates balanced disputes against other pre-candidates such as Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (UB).

item.title: A disputa pela Presidência no 1º turno, segundo novo Datafolha
item.description: Lula leads the first round with 39%, technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (35%) following the PSD’s announcement of Ronaldo Caiado as its pre-candidate. The Datafolha poll shows stable rejection rates: 48% against Lula and 46% against Flávio. In a potential runoff, Flávio narrowly leads with 46% versus Lula’s 45%, reversing the March trend where Lula was ahead.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula registra 48% de rejeição enquanto Flávio tem 46%
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows Lula with 48% rejection and Flávio Bolsonaro with 46%, keeping both at the top of rejection among pre-candidates. In a hypothetical runoff, Lula would have 45% and Flávio 46%, a technical tie within the two-point margin of error. Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado follow with 17% and 16% rejection, respectively.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula empata com Flávio, Caiado e Zema no 2º turno
item.description: Lula is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (45% vs 46%), Romeu Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado (both 45% vs 42%) in second-round scenarios, according to Datafolha. The two-point margin of error keeps all results within statistical equality. Caiado rose from 36% to 42% since the March poll after being confirmed as the PSD's presidential candidate.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 46% contra 45% de Lula no 2º turno
item.description: A Datafolha poll from April 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 46% and Lula (PT) at 45% in a hypothetical second-round scenario, representing a technical tie within the two-point margin of error. This marks the first time the Bolsonaro-aligned senator has led the president in a Datafolha survey. In the first-round scenario, Lula leads with 39%, followed by Bolsonaro at 35%.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno em novo Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on April 11, 2026 shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a potential presidential runoff, with the senator numerically ahead at 46% versus 45% for the president. The margin of error is two percentage points. The poll also included alternative scenarios with Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo), both tied with Lula at 45% to 42%.

item.title: Eleição no Rio gera cabo de guerra no Supremo
item.description: The succession race for Rio de Janeiro’s governor is causing tensions in Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court, pitting supporters of indirect elections against advocates of direct popular vote. The outcome may hinge on Jorge Messias, whose STF nomination is advancing in the Senate, with a confirmation hearing set for April 29. The stalemate aims to delay a ruling until supplementary elections become unfeasible before the October general vote, with the TSE citing a resolution allowing a single election in October.

item.title: Empresário investigado por atos golpistas de 8 de janeiro é preso pelo ICE nos EUA
item.description: Esdras Jônatas dos Santos, a businessman investigated for involvement in the January 8, 2023, coup attempts, was arrested by ICE in the United States and is being held in Florida. He has an active arrest warrant in Brazil for leading anti-democratic protests in Minas Gerais following the 2022 elections and claims to have been in the U.S. since the attacks. U.S. authorities confirmed his detention, though deportation is not automatic and depends on ongoing immigration proceedings.

item.title: Lula quer incluir devedores do Fies em novo programa de renegociação de dívidas
item.description: President Lula announced that the government plans to include Fies student loan defaulters in a new debt renegotiation program aimed at easing household indebtedness and supporting youth professional training. The initiative, still under development, may be launched in the coming days and is part of a broader package that includes potential use of FGTS funds to settle debts. Lula stressed that regularizing these debts is crucial so students can become qualified professionals and contribute to national development.

item.title: O que se fala nos bastidores sobre a possibilidade de Lula não disputar eleição
item.description: Lula has not yet decided whether to run for re-election in 2026, reflecting a strategic dilemma between his desire to run and the risk of a symbolic defeat to Flávio Bolsonaro, heir to Bolsonarism. Allies indicate his hesitation is not merely rhetorical but a real calculation of electoral cost and the historical impact of a potential loss. The PT’s grassroots mobilization has weakened, making voter decisions increasingly dependent on individual economic perceptions.

item.title: Haddad lança estratégia para enfrentar Tarcísio nos debates e nas urnas
item.description: Fernando Haddad is launching a campaign to challenge Tarcísio de Freitas in the São Paulo gubernatorial race, highlighting his achievements as mayor and minister—such as bike lanes, Prouni, and tax exemptions for those earning up to R$5,000—while attempting to counter criticisms over tax increases during his tenure at the Finance Ministry, particularly the 'tax on small imports,' which he claims targeted the wealthy.

item.title: Kátia Abreu espera conversa com Lula sobre seu papel na eleição do Tocantins
item.description: Kátia Abreu, former Agriculture Minister and senator, announced her affiliation with the PT and said she hopes to speak with Lula to define her role in Tocantins’ elections. She denied plans to run for state governor, saying she is working to build a strong platform to support Lula in the state. Her party switch surprised local politics, given her long history in center-right parties like PP, DEM, and as leader of the agribusiness lobby.

item.title: Jair Bolsonaro deixou um precedente e uma dica eleitoral para Lula
item.description: Lula aims to reduce voter dissatisfaction with the cost of living through fuel subsidies, tax exemptions, and higher taxes on cigarettes and oil exports, with an estimated cost of up to 31 billion reais. He also plans to use presidential authority and public resources to distribute benefits such as income tax exemption for those earning up to R$5,000 monthly, cooking gas for 15 million families, and reduced or zero electricity bills for 60 million families — strategies similar to those employed by Bolsonaro in 2022 to overcome polling deficits.

item.title: A reação nada amigável de ministros do STF a falas de Lula sobre Moraes e o Vorcaro
item.description: Some STF ministers close to Lula expressed dissatisfaction with his criticisms of Alexandre de Moraes' biography and demands for the Court to explain ties between its members and banker Daniel Vorcaro. One justice said Lula's remarks reflect anxiety over his electoral struggles and re-election prospects, calling them unfair and driven by fear of losing the election.

item.title: Divisão no STF sobre RJ antecipa clima de eleições e desenha aliança Kassio-Mendonça
item.description: The STF is divided over whether to hold direct elections for governor of Rio de Janeiro, with ministers Kassio Nunes Marques and André Mendonça opposing the idea that the Supreme Court should review TSE decisions, while Alexandre de Moraes, Gilmar Mendes, Flávio Dino and Cristiano Zanin support direct elections as an exceptional measure. The lack of consensus led to a request for vista, postponing the decision and keeping Ricardo Couto as acting governor, excluding the PL from power. The conflict reveals tensions between the STF and TSE that foreshadow the political climate of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Como Ricardo Nunes vai colaborar no plano de governo de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes announced he will contribute to Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential government plan in three areas: urban security, through replicating the Smart Sampa program; food security, via initiatives like Armazém Solidário and community kitchens; and public transportation, by transitioning to an electric bus fleet.

item.title: As reações no STF após tentativa de Lula de se descolar da crise que atinge a Corte
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's attempt to distance himself from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) during the Banco Master crisis provoked an immediate negative reaction from the Court, with his public criticism of Minister Alexandre de Moraes seen as an opportunistic move to shift political blame onto the judiciary. The statement backfired, being interpreted as a sign of fear over losing the election rather than a genuine assertion of independence, further straining the already deteriorating relationship between the Executive and Judicial branches.

item.title: Goleada e denúncia de racismo: Brasil vence a Argentina e garante vaga no Mundial Sub-17
item.description: Brazil defeated Argentina 3-0 in the U-17 South American Championship, securing an early berth for the 2026 World Cup with goals from Riquelme (2) and Eduardo Conceição. However, the match was overshadowed by an alleged racist gesture by an Argentine player toward the Brazilian bench, which the referee failed to act upon under anti-racism protocols, leading to post-match tensions. Despite the incident, Brazil resumed celebrations after technical staff intervened.

item.title: PT aciona o TSE contra vídeos de IA que simulam violência contra mulheres
item.description: The PT filed a representation with the TSE against AI-generated videos simulating violence against its female militants, including physical assaults and hate messages. The party will also send extrajudicial notices to platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook to remove the content.
